commit.message:
feat(post)!: the document's unit is the unit every post writes the program in

The document's Units choice (SetUnits, saved as `units`) is now the
program's unit too - one setting, never the machine file's. The app
states it to every post as postOptions.Units ("mm" / "inch"); the
engine refuses an inch document on a script whose manifest does not
declare programUnits = "mm inch", by name, before any hook runs.

- Fanuc, Haas, Mazak, Doosan DNM (G20) and Siemens 840D (G700) write
  inch: lengths / 25.4 at four decimals, feeds in in/min at two; angles,
  seconds and rpm unchanged. The three Tormach posts read the document
  instead of machine.units.
- Makera Carvera (mm-only firmware), Heidenhain and Fanuc Lathe refuse
  an inch document by name (the latter two pending verified inch work).
- PROJECT_VERSION 59: an older project opens on the unit its programs
  posted in (from its machine files), with a load note when its display
  changes, so it posts byte-identical.
- Post section shows a "Program units" row (same SetUnits as the Stock
  page); the post status line names the unit.
- MCP: set_units tool; get_job reports units. post.exe: --units.

BREAKING CHANGE: a new document on an inch machine file (the shipped
Tormach machines) now posts mm until the document is set to inch;
v59 project files are refused by older builds.

Fixes #902

feat(post): Fanuc Lathe writes inch programs from the document's unit

An inch document now posts on the Fanuc Lathe post as G20 instead of
being refused: programUnits = "mm inch", and every word is converted
where it is written (the stream and all geometry checks stay mm).

- Lengths (X diameter, Z, I K, G76 R, tool note) / 25.4 at four
  decimals; G99 feed per rev in in/rev; thread leads (G32 / G76 F) in
  inches at six decimals.
- No-point increment words (G76 P Q, G83 Q peck) in 0.0001 in, where
  mm counts microns.
- G96 S in surface feet per minute (m/min / 0.3048); G97 / G50 rpm,
  dwell ms and the G76 P(m)(r)(a) code never scale.
- The PART LOAD advance comment names inches.
- Refused by name: a C-axis live-tool section on an inch program (its
  composite rotary feed under G20 is not confirmed from a public
  source), a per-rev feed that rounds to F0, a G76 depth under the
  least increment.

mm output is byte-identical: every committed mm golden is unchanged
and re-checked by the new lathe_post_inch suite, which also commits
inch goldens (facing, rough + finish, groove + part, axial drill, G76
and G32 threads) checked word by word against their mm twins.

Fixes #977

fix(post): angle words never take the document unit; tinyg follows the unit law

Main's angleWord (Fanuc, Doosan DNM, #997) wrote through `w`, which this
change made the unit-aware length word: an inch program would have
divided A/B/C by 25.4. It writes degrees through `wa` (resolved in the
merge). Pinned by program_units::rotary_angle_words_are_degrees_in_an_inch_program
(RTCP arm and walk on the tilthead for both posts, Doosan's index path);
with `w` back in angleWord it fails (A1.4764 for A37.5).

grblHAL and TinyG (new on main) read machine.units: they now take the
program unit from postOptions.Units and declare programUnits = "mm inch"
(their inch path already scaled lengths and feeds). Pinned by
program_units::grbl_family_posts_write_the_mm_program_in_inches and the
updated tinyg_post / grblhal_post inch tests.

The six inch drill_peck goldens re-recorded after #994 (G99 and the
return move to R); no other golden moved.

Refs #902
